subject: treasureHoard
pitch:
Category: Prop group.
Subject: treasure hoard: coins, gems, chest, crown, goblets.
Style: League of Legends.
reasoning:
Analyzing the request reveals a prop group for a treasure hoard, focusing on coins, gems, chest, crown, and goblets. The desired style is "League of Legends," which implies hand-painted, stylized, heroic fantasy elements, including chunky proportions, bold silhouettes, rich textures with warm gold highlights and deep shadows, magical glowing gems, and runic/ornate filigree.


The "League of Legends" style guide necessitates a faceted, low-poly aesthetic that contrasts with the initial instinct for realistic detail.  Starting with the dungeon base, broken flagstones with runes will be the starting point. The goal is to create a dynamic composition with texture and visual interest, which will be achieved through the use of the appropriate color palette.


Focus shifts to defining the specific props: a dramatic treasure chest overflowing with gold and jewels, a regal crown atop the hoard, chunky goblets (one tipped), and oversized, glowing gemstones. The coin pile should be a lumpy organic mound with individual coins scattered around. Finally, I'll add a heroic dagger or sword hilt.


Planning to incorporate details such as necklaces draped over the chest and neatly stacked gold ingots to enrich the scene's visual appeal. Defining the construction plan involves using a specified SDK for 3D object creation. The goal is a rich scene within the part and triangle budget, starting with an octagonal stone dais at y=0, featuring a cracked texture and velvet runner. The treasure chest will be positioned slightly off-center and angled.


Considering detailed chest construction: iron-reinforced bronze corner plates, curved bracket fittings with rivets, heavy gold trims, and a keyhole escutcheon are required. The lid will be an arched barrel design, with dark wood slats inside and gold reinforcement. The interior will contain an organic gold mound with a mix of individual coins and gold ingots. The coins will have a crest stamp on them.


Adding gold bars, a royal crown, and various goblets to the treasure composition, focusing on distinctive "League of Legends" design cues. The crown will feature filigree, inset gems, flared spires, and a central glowing gem, while the goblets will include upright and overturned variations, showcasing ornate details. Oversized, faceted gemstones will be implemented, with specific geometry and glow effects for enhanced visual impact.


Considering gem placement; inside the chest, spilling out, caught on the rim and tucked within goblets. Adding pearl necklaces and jeweled chains, using bezier curves for draping. Exploring an ornate dagger or relic blade to add heroic element to the scene.

Refining dimensions, defining scene boundaries, dais base, chest size with lid angle. Specifying crown dimensions and placement along with precise goblet measurements. Detailing ingot and coin sizes with gem ranges and scaling.


Defining material properties for the scene elements: Gold paint will use a metallic gradient with specific color codes and simulate League's hand-painted style with edge highlights. Dark bog oak, dark iron/slate hardware, and velvet fabric will be assigned respective colors and textures.

Establishing the scene's skeleton, a master root joint ("treasury") at the origin will control the prop group, with optional joints for movable parts like the chest lid. Considering SDK constraints: only one root joint is permitted for proper function.


A root joint is being established at the origin to serve as the master control. SDK constraints are reviewed, specifically limitations on parts, triangles, joints, colors, and the requirement for the model to stand on the y=0 plane. The dais and flooring are being constructed starting with an octagonal stone plinth, stepped rim, and flagstones. A velvet runner will also be created with a curved path.


Chest placement is determined with center coordinates and rotation defined, along with overall dimensions for base, with beveled posts, dark oak panels, claw feet, gold straps, lion-head handles, and keyhole escutcheon. Lid hinge location and angle are specified with arched wooden construction, gold ribs, an open clasp, and a chain connecting to the interior.


Constructing the coin pile involves three distinct elements: an ellipsoidal mound within the chest, a flowing cascade over the edge, and a spreading pool on the floor, all utilizing a specific gold material. Individual coins will be chunky cylinders with a stamped crest, arranged in stacks and scattered loosely. Gold ingots will be stacked with tapered sides, stylized to align with the "League of Legends" aesthetic.


Detailed ingot placement and specifications are being incorporated, along with a grand royal crown featuring a filigree base, inset gems, and a glowing ruby. The crown's position, rotation, and dimensions are defined, including its velvet cap and finial details. Upright goblets and chalices are also positioned, along with height and base dimensions.


Goblet details are being refined, including specific shapes, materials (gold, pearl studs), and contents (glowing liquid). The tipped goblet's position and spilling gem stream are being determined. Gemstone geometry is defined, specifying faceted shapes (e.g., octahedron, rhombus) with specific colors and glow effects based on the "League of Legends" style. Distinct gems, such as a "Hextech Arcane Crystal," are being assigned locations within the scene, with specific color values.


Planning a specific placement for roughly 15-20 glowing gems. Defining pearl necklace construction with Bezier curves.  Adding a ruby and gold beaded chain for a goblet.

Incorporating a ceremonial dagger with specified dimensions and placement. The dagger features a lion-head pommel, leather grip with gold wire, winged crossguard, and cyan glowing runic blade.

Custom SVG textures are being created for coins, filigree, runes, and ingots.  Custom gold paint is being formulated with specified light and noise.


Material definitions are being refined, including specific color values and gradients for bog oak, dark iron, stone, and a layered gold effect with amber recesses. Part counts are estimated and budgets are checked, concluding that the plan is well within the allocated limits of 1000 parts. I'll utilize low-to-medium poly primitives to stay within the triangle budget, estimating a total of 15k-25k triangles within the 60k budget. The color palette will be kept under 32 colors.


Scene coordinate system is confirmed, with +Y up, +Z forward, and +X left, also confirming object placement relative to y=0. Code imports from 3D library and build toolkit are verified for accuracy.
I'm thinking through how to approach this.
